recap.text: Carl and Donut find a Gate Pass signed by Magistrate Featherfall and a letter in necroscript. They learn Featherfall is a boss man who lives in a town hall with a clerk named Miss Quill. Carl blows up the floor and finds Featherfall's emaciated, naked body lashed upside down in a bone dreamcatcher. Miss Quill killed Featherfall with spell feedback to take control of the city.

beats.headline: A pass signed in his name
beats.text: Two pieces of paper from the quest. A Gate Pass: "The holder of this pass is doing this on my orders. Magistrate Featherfall." Carrying it keeps the mindless swordsman guards off your back, provided your criminal enterprise is not too overt and you stay in the township that issued it. Beside it lies a blood-soaked letter in necroscript, which Mordecai cannot read but recognises: something an undead magic user writes. His conclusion: "I'm thinking you two might have a lich problem."
beats.gist: Magistrate Featherfall is the magistrate of a skyfowl settlement.

beats.headline: He cares about being disturbed
beats.text: Mordecai's briefing: the surviving skyfowl villages keep the old structure without the oversight, so Featherfall is this village's big boss man. Getting to him means teleporting onto the town hall's third-floor landing and walking through a mall for skyfowl. His clerk, Miss Quill, declines to disturb him about a dead woman who is not skyfowl; it was like this under her late husband, and it is like this now with Magistrate Featherfall. The door to his chambers is magically locked.
beats.gist: Magistrate Featherfall is a skyfowl boss man whose clerk, Miss Quill, refuses to disturb him.

beats.headline: A dark cleric, in theory
beats.text: The working theory, formed after an attack by shambling berserkers that Crawler Carl assumes were sent by "our Featherfall friend." The town's lead skyfowl is a dark cleric who commands the undead. The city elves of the 201st Security Group worship the skyfowl as living angels, which makes them free, enthusiastic labour for herding his undead minions. Knock out that support network first. Nobody has yet explained the dead women in the alleys.
beats.gist: Magistrate Featherfall is a dark cleric who commands undead minions and is worshipped by city elves.

beats.headline: Credited with his death
beats.text: Dynamite through the magistrate's floor. The notices arrive: a public official assassinated, control of the Medium Skyfowl Settlement, a new title, Magistrate Carl. The only NPC the notices name is Miss Quill, and a bronze boss box says one of the two was a neighbourhood boss. But the quest is still open, which should mean the head bad guy is still alive. Crawler Carl's conclusion: they killed an NPC they never met, blew his house to bits, and still have not finished the job.
beats.gist: Carl blows dynamite through Magistrate Featherfall's floor and becomes Magistrate Carl of the Medium Skyfowl Settlement.

beats.headline: Upside down in a bone dreamcatcher
beats.text: Found in the magistrate's quarters, at the centre of a room of krasue bodies hanging from the ceiling: Magistrate Featherfall, naked and emaciated, lashed upside down in a massive dreamcatcher of bone, featherless wings spread, a clear fluid dripping from beak and eyes. He had been there some time; the body was being mummified. Lootable Corpse. Former Magistrate Featherfall. Dark Cleric. Level 32. A fireball scatters his ashes. No neighbourhood map turns up in them, so by Crawler Carl's reckoning he was not the boss.
beats.gist: Carl finds Magistrate Featherfall naked and emaciated, lashed upside down in a bone dreamcatcher.

beats.headline: A dark fetish, by her account
beats.text: A dying krasue woman, mortal while Crawler Donut's torch holds the curse back, sets the record straight. Featherfall was not the one who did this. He has been hanging on that thing the whole time, and he was dead when she arrived. His body was turned into a dark fetish that keeps their bodies safe at night. Miss Quill has been running the city all along. She is the real magistrate.
beats.gist: A krasue woman says Miss Quill is the real magistrate and Featherfall is a dark fetish.

beats.headline: Killed by the feedback
beats.text: Remex, Soul Leech Capacitor, tells it as a story he has rehearsed. Featherfall never liked the guards and wanted more control over them; after Remex retired and handed him the perch, he asked what it would take. After Remex died, Featherfall asked Quill to help cast a spell that would pull a dark cleric back from the dim as a capacitor. He took the Night Votive position with Quill in the room, too close to the amplifier. The feedback killed him. Quill planned it. She kept his office running with a forgery spell.
beats.gist: Featherfall dies from feedback after Quill plans a spell to pull a dark cleric from the dim.
